question: Infosys SP / System Engineer technical interview. Reported topics: **operator overloading with an example versus function overriding**, **friend functions**, and **header files in C**. The round also covered OOP, DBMS, SDLC and basic SQL.
lookingFor: Distinguishing overloading (compile time) from overriding (runtime) correctly.
Writing a short, valid C++ operator overload.
Understanding friend and the encapsulation trade-off.
Knowing what header files do in the C compilation model.
followUps: Why is operator<< usually overloaded as a friend or non-member function?
What is the difference between a header file and a library?
What happens if you forget include guards?
Can constructors be virtual? Why or why not?
